answer: Verifiers on the bridge ledger post a bond and countersign transactions; if they approve an invalid one, the ledger automatically slashes a penalty priced above any full epoch reward. A fake-identity attacker farming a garden of cheap agent IDs gains nothing unless every identity holds real capital, and any caught fraud costs more than months of honest harbor fees. So sybil farming is irrational: upfront bonds per identity plus guaranteed loss exceeding total possible payoff, not mere discouragement.
